Hello Nsu Peeps! This is my first ever faculty review post.
Mhcw (Mgt314)- Sir's lecture is amazing. Sir explained every concept deeply. If you have aim to major in SCM, you can go to his section. Sir's quiz is tricky as you have to clear the concepts by 100%. Mids and Finals are super easy, just practice maths from slide. 90% of questions of mids and final are math. So if you love math, go to him. Your report must contain topics sir given in instructions. He curves also.
Squ (Che101)- Mam is super easygoing. She makes this course very easy for students. Slides are so easy. All questions will come directly from slides. Mam will tell in class which slides are important. You have to note down that. Which problems are given in slides, in exam there will be same problems just with changed digits. Exam questions are very easy. No assignments and group project. Mam curves one grade. A sweet faculty with good heart who always motivates her students.
Rqr (Fin410)- Sir is very cool and chill. He treated his students as his brothers and sisters. Classes will be very fun and interesting. Sir teach finance always given relevance examples from industry. Quizzes, Mid 1 and Final are easy. Maths come directly from the slides with changed digits. Mid 2 is very difficult. If you get a good mark in mid 2 you'll definitely get a good grade. Mcqs will be taken from students in a doc file and will be repeated in exam. There also have bonus problems. A major course can be passed with minimal effort and comfort I won't get it if hadn't go for Rqr Sir. Sir curves a lot!
Lkk (Bus251)- Mam is very strict in terms of rules and punctuality. Exam questions are easy. But answers must be match with mam's instructions in lectures. Otherwise mam will deduct marks. Mam checked the report seriously. If you want to get a good grade you must work on your report very carefully by following mam's instructions. Presentations must be natural-speaking presentation. Avoid reading from slides and phones. Don't miss any classes because you'll regret. Mam said she won't curve but she curved 2 grades at last.

text:
Faculty reviews - Summer 2024

MGT314 - MdRH (Dr. Mohammad Rashidul Hassan)

One of the most humble faculties I've come across to date. Sir teaches well and in a very detailed manner. However, I found his lectures to be a bit slow. He took three quizzes and counted the best two. The first quiz had definitions and T/F questions. The rest of the quizzes were based on maths only. There were two mids. In the first mid, he gave two theoretical and two mathematical questions. In the second mid, there was one theoretical question and three maths. The final had four mathematical questions. In all of these exams, we had to answer three questions. His theoretical questions were not the easiest, as he made them in such a way that connected theories with real-world applications. So, only memorizing the theories from the book won't guarantee good marks. The maths, on the other hand, were very straightforward. He will highlight maths from the book, and you will face exactly the same or similar maths in the exams. He took one group assignment and gave plenty of time to submit. Finally, he curved based on the section's overall performance.

BUS173 - MHM (Mr. Md. Hannan Miah)

[If you are looking for an easygoing faculty, simply avoid MHM]

Hands down one of the BESTEST stats faculties of all time. Sir teaches exceptionally well. He took a total of six quizzes and counted the best five. This means you'll have to sit for a quiz after finishing each chapter. Taking the quizzes seriously will increase your chance of getting good marks in the mids and the final. Some of the quizzes had MCQs, and some had direct maths. Both of the mids and the final each was worth 100 marks (10 MCQs and 4 maths). All of the questions were based on his lectures. Sometimes, you might find some unconventional questions, but if your concept is clear, you'll have no issues solving those. He marks generously, too. He allows formula sheets to be taken in the exams. Unlike other faculties, he won't ask you to solve tedious calculations in Regression. Instead, he will show you the application using Excel and SPSS. Besides these, he will show how to conduct all of the tests taught in this course using SPSS. In his course structure, he kept a section worth 15 marks where we had to visit his office and show how to do data analysis with regression, chi-square, ANOVA, and conduct non-parametric tests such as sign test, Wilcoxon signed rank test, Mann-Whitney test, etc. using SPSS. He might shift to Stata starting next semester as it is a superior software. After being done with all these, he will teach the fundamental concepts of time-series analysis and forecasting (basically moving average, weighted moving average, and exponential smoothing covered in MGT314. This topic isn't taught by the overwhelming majority of the faculties of BUS173). All in all, if you are a sincere student and actually want to learn *applied* statistics from someone who grades fairly, Hannan sir is a fantastic choice.

PBH101 - SKMF (Dr. Shomik Maruf)

An absolute king. There are very good reasons why sir is one of the best-reviewed Public Health faculty members at NSU. He teaches well and makes the classes very engaging. He took three quizzes and counted the best two. The quizzes included short questions, MCQs, T/F, and matching. The questions in the mid were similar. But there were only short questions in the final. If you read all of the slides properly, scoring very good marks in the exams should be fairly easy. Make sure to do well on the quizzes to get a good grade. One thing to note is that groups will be formed in the very first class, and you will sit for group quizzes. This means groupmates can communicate with each other while attending the quizzes. He took individual assignments and group presentations and graded them very leniently. Lastly, he might even curve based on your individual efforts and the section's overall performance.

ECO201 - MUK (Dr. Md. Syeed Uz Zaman Khan)

This is not an easy course by any means. I personally found the jump from ECO101 to ECO201 to be pretty steep. However, Syeed sir teaches well and doesn't delve into the nitty gritty parts of the syllabus. Instead, he keeps the lectures short and focuses on the basics of the topics. Getting a good grade from him requires attending all of the classes, taking notes, and reading the book (this one is crucial). He took two quizzes and counted both this semester. Unlike other semesters, he took one mid. All of the exams included written questions; some were straightforward theoretical questions, and some were mathematical questions. The quizzes consisted of three questions, and we had to answer two. In the mid and the final, he gave five questions, and we had to answer three. The hardest part of this course was his relatively unforgiving percentage distribution. He took the mid worth 30 marks and converted it to 35, and again, he took the final worth 30 marks but converted it to 45. So, losing even a single mark had a heavy toll on our overall grades. Lastly, he doesn't curve. So, you must remain consistent with your marks throughout the entire semester if you are aiming for a good grade.

ECO204- JVHn (Dr. Javed Hossain)

GOAT. Sir is just a chill guy xD. He teaches very well, and his lectures are fun to attend. He took two quizzes and dropped one, and there was only one mid. All of the exams were mostly based on short questions. The mid and the final had a few T/F questions that required explanations of the answers. I personally found the mid to be pretty easy, but the final was relatively more complicated. He took two individual assignments and two in-class group assignments. The group assignments were enjoyable, and sir was very cooperative while completing those. Getting a good grade from him isn't too tough (he curves as well). Just attend all of the classes, take notes, and read the book. You don't need to read the book rigorously. It's just to make sure that your overall understanding of the concepts is solidified. Do learn the derivations properly, as he loves to include those in the exams.

The timings of all of the faculties can be found here: nsu.app
